judgments.reasoning_cat1: The split between discounts that 'accrue to the Owner' and those that 'otherwise accrue to the Contractor' turns on conditions (payment already reimbursed, funds deposited) that are stated but fact-sensitive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 9.1.1 [New] adds a seven-day notice regime before the Contractor may take any discount for itself, which qualifies this clause and must be read with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single mechanical crediting rule; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1 and with the Cost of the Work accounting in Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Those portions of the Work that the Contractor does not customarily perform with the Contractor's own personnel' is a soft self-performance boundary, and 'reasonable objection' is a standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 6.5 imposes its own bidding procedure (at least two bids, Owner-named subcontractors) and A201 5.2 a different approval mechanism, so the award process is stated in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise formula for a Change Order when the Owner rejects the recommended bidder.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adjusts the Guaranteed Maximum Price, which 5.2.1 leaves as 'N/A', and Addendum 6.5 supplies a parallel Change Order route for bid pricing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A monthly billing period with an unfilled 'or as follows' alternative; the default is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with 12.1.3 and A201 9.3.1; no inconsistency identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fill-in dates are garbled and partly indeterminate ('not later than the ___ day of a month', 'the first day of the following month', 'fifteen days'), which is exactly the sort of mechanical defect that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.3.1 (application ten days before the payment date), 9.4.1 (certificate within seven days) and 9.6.1 must be fitted to these dates, and A201 9.7.1's seven-day non-payment trigger depends on them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed substantiation formula with clear arithmetic; 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect' is a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum adds a differently-worded 12.1.4 [New] with lien waivers and subcontractor statements, so the same number carries two provisions that must be read cumulatively.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the schedule of values to allocate 'the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price' — a figure the Agreement never supplies — and makes the Architect the arbiter of form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.1 leaves the Guaranteed Maximum Price as 'N/A' while Addendum 6.5 substitutes a Preliminary Budget and itemized Schedule of Values keyed to the Contract Sum; the two schemes do not align.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'lesser of' formula is precise but is expressed as a share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With no GMP stated in 5.2.1, this computation has no denominator; Addendum 6.5's evolving Schedule of Values is the only substitute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A truncated lead-in to the payment computation; nothing substantive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces subclauses that all rest on the missing Guaranteed Maximum Price.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical arithmetic tied to percentages of completion; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It multiplies percentages by 'the share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocated to that portion of the Work', which cannot be done under a contract whose GMP is 'N/A'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds stored-materials value with an advance-approval condition; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same dependence on the unstated Guaranteed Maximum Price; otherwise consistent with 7.5.6 and A201 9.3.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retainage percentage is entered as 'N/A' while the clause directs a deduction of that percentage, and it offers alternative fee computations (rate versus fixed sum) without saying which applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.7.3 [Revision] substitutes five percent retainage, so the executed instrument carries two versions of this subclause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line subtraction; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Standard and consistent with 12.1.7 and 13.2.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shortfall ... or resulting from errors subsequently discovered by the Owner's accountants' is broad but tied to a defined documentation requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 12.1.4 and Article 11 accounting records; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cross-referenced deduction for withheld certification; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches A201 9.5.1; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subparagraph is mis-numbered 12.1.9 (duplicating the next one) and sets subcontractor retainage at 'not less than ten percent' while leaving the procedure to future agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.7.3 fixes the Contractor's own retainage at five percent, and A201 9.6.2 requires payment reflecting percentages 'actually retained', so the retainage scheme is split across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional disclaimer of the Architect's verification duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 9.4.2 and Article 11 audit rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in stating the two conditions for final payment; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.2.1 [New] adds a third condition (recorded Notice of Completion), so the conditions are stated in two places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other requirements, if any, which extend beyond final payment' is a small open end in an otherwise plain condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with A201 12.2.2 and 9.10.2; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.2.3 and A201 9.10.1; Addendum 9.10.1.1 adds a warranties precondition to issuance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Thirty days after the final Certificate 'or as follows:' with the alternative left blank — an incomplete term on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision] replaces this with fifty days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or five days after a lien-free endorsement, a materially different trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed time periods with an express supersession of A201 9.4.1; carefully drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its timetable must be squared with Addendum 12.2.2's Notice-of-Completion trigger and with A201 9.10.1's prompt-issuance duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives a 30-day arbitration demand right 'without a further decision of the Architect' and makes failure to demand binding — a forfeiture provision whose scope ('the disputed amount') is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.5.1/4.6.1 make mediation and prior submission to the Architect conditions precedent to arbitration, and A201 4.6.3 sets different time limits, so the routes to arbitration conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement of post-final-payment correction costs 'but not in excess of the Guaranteed Maximum Price', plus a savings recalculation, both keyed to figures not supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no GMP in 5.2.1 and no savings-participation provision was inserted at Paragraph 5.2, so two of this clause's premises are missing from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap ('shall not exceed the amount the Contractor would be entitled to receive under Paragraph 13.2') coupled with a Fee 'calculated as if the Work had been fully completed' is an awkward, arguably self-defeating combination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.4.3 promises payment for Work executed plus overhead and profit on Work not executed, which this Agreement caps differently; the two payment measures must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear cap formula introduced by a cross-reference to A201 14.2.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cap is 'shall not cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded', a limit the Agreement never quantifies, and A201 14.2.4 provides its own accounting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single arithmetic step.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 7 and 13.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Offers two alternative fee computations without stating which one the executed 5.1.2 triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.1.2 states a lump sum whose words and figures appear inconsistent, so this ratio computation depends on a contested number.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line subtraction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Article 13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair compensation, either by purchase or rental at the election of the Owner' leaves the measure of compensation undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Exhibit A's equipment rental rates and 7.5.2, which supply rates that could or could not measure 'fair compensation'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise substitution of 'Contractor's Fee' for 'profit' in the A201 suspension clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It increases 'the Guaranteed Maximum Price', which does not exist here, and references 6.4's equitable fee adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general rule that references incorporate amendments; drafted with a missing word ('a provision AIA Document A201') but the sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the bridge between the Agreement, the Addendum and the Supplementary Conditions, and cuts against Article 1's 'this Agreement shall govern' precedence rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The interest rate blank is unfilled, leaving only 'the legal rate prevailing ... at the place where the Project is located', which is itself indeterminate in Hawaii practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.7.1 also promises interest 'as provided for in the Contract Documents', so the unfilled rate matters elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens' and 'Mary Williamson' without saying whether authority is joint or several.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 14.3 [Revised] and Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 give two further, differently worded designations (Mary Williamson as authorized representative; actions by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson), so three provisions describe the same office differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies one representative 'succeeded by' another, leaving the timing and effect of the succession unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14.5 requires ten days' notice for any change of representative, and Addendum Article 2 [Revised] requires designation of a supervisory employee responsible for the project, which may or may not be the same person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite notice requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with 14.3, 14.4 and Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1, which name representatives without addressing the notice mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other provisions:' is left blank, so it has no content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.1 excepts personnel costs 'as may be provided in Article 14', which the blank never supplies, and the Addendum inserts an entirely different 14.6 [New].

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare enumeration lead-in.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its list determines what Article 1 makes binding; the list itself is incomplete in later subparagraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Agreement as the executed 1997 A111; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 15.1.1 [Revision] restates it 'as modified by the First Addendum', which supersedes this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It identifies 'the 1991 edition' of the General Conditions while naming AIA Document A201-1997 in the same sentence — an internal date mismatch that changes which document is incorporated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 15.1.2 [Revision] and the Supplementary Conditions both say the 1997 edition as modified, so the enumeration and the modifying documents disagree on their face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Specifications are identified only by reference to a Project Manual 'dated as in Subparagraph 15.1.3', which is itself marked TBD, and the list is blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 and A201 1.1.1 make Specifications binding Contract Documents, so a blank enumeration leaves the scope of the Work anchored to undocumented papers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Drawings 'are as follows' with no drawings listed and a garbled date, so the document that defines the Work is unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 1.1.5, 1.2.1 and 3.2.1 all assume identified Drawings, and Addendum 6.5 contemplates further 'Preliminary Drawings', so the enumeration cannot be squared with the fast-track scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists the two addenda and excludes bidding-requirement portions; reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms that the First Addendum and Supplementary Conditions are Contract Documents, which activates the precedence question in Article 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumeration of Exhibits A-E buried in AIA instructional text; the listing itself is short but the exhibits' status as pricing terms is not explained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits A, C and D add charges (equipment rates, a 5% hand-tool adder, a 1% insurance rate, excise tax) that Article 7 and 8.1.7 do not expressly authorise, so their incorporation creates the tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Article 16 contains only the AIA instruction and no limits of liability or bond requirements, so the article is empty where the form calls for terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 11.1.2 requires insurance 'for not less than limits ... specified in the Contract Documents or required by law', and Exhibit D/E supply only a premium rate and a certificate, so the required limits are never stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard execution and counterparts recital, partly garbled by scanning but plain in sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Addendum and Supplementary Conditions have their own undated signature blocks, a mismatch of execution formalities rather than an operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital of incorporation that dates the Agreement 'February 1, 2002' and states the Addendum's purpose; the language itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's own opening recites it is made as of the first day of an unstated month in 2002 and the Addendum's execution date is blank, so recital and operative dating diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only skilled and properly trained staff', 'appropriately skilled and experienced supervisory employee' and work that 'does not impair his or her ability to perform this Work' are qualitative standards with no benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlays A201 3.9.1's superintendent requirement and Supplementary Condition 3.10.4-3.10.5 on schedule maintenance, which assign overlapping duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pending approval of permits' is undefined — it may be a condition, a permitted delay, or mere background — and it qualifies the only fixed commencement date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1 makes commencement the date of the Agreement unless otherwise stated, 4.2 measures Contract Time from commencement, and A201 8.1.2 defines it by the Agreement, so a conditional date unsettles the whole time scheme.
